segments.title: 第40章 顏竹笙
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 40 Yan Zhusheng

The girl who walked in seemed to bring a gust of cold wind with her.

She wore a clean white shirt and a pair of washed-out, faded jeans, her legs straight and slender, making her appear very tall.

When Li Luo turned to look at her, even at his height of 1.75 meters, he felt he was almost at eye level with her.

But he wasn't just looking to see what she looked like.

It was simply because he seemed to recognize the girl's name.

After he turned and saw her face clearly, he swore under his breath.

"Yes, give me your admission notice and school fees." Kong Junxiang, however, was calm as he pointed to the student roster in front of him. "Just sign here."

"Okay." Yan Zhusheng nodded lightly, and the high ponytail at the back of her head swayed gently, the tips of her hair tapping her back.

By now, Li Luo had already looked away and walked down from the podium, taking a seat by the window in the back row. His gaze drifted to the girl bending over the podium to sign her name, thinking to himself that such a coincidence could actually happen in this world.

What's it like to be classmates with your boss from your previous life after being reborn?

Li Luo's lips twitched.

To think that the musical prodigy who needed help even to shoot short videos in his past life was once also a student at Fuyi High?

Looking at that cool, delicate oval face, Li Luo sighed inwardly. He then watched as Yan Zhusheng finished signing her name and walked down from the podium, getting closer and closer, finally arriving at the seat next to him. "Is this seat taken?"

Li Luo shook his head, indicating that no one was sitting there.

But being desk mates with his boss from a past life, even if only temporarily, felt a little strange to Li Luo, so he pointed to an empty seat in front of them and asked, "Why don't you sit at the front?"

Yan Zhusheng shook her head and pulled out the chair to sit next to Li Luo. "I'm quite tall. Sitting at the front would block other people's view."

Hearing her say that, Li Luo just nodded in acknowledgement and didn't speak further, briefly sinking into his memories.

He vaguely remembered that in his past life, he was already in his early thirties.

The market for short dramas was saturated, the competition for screenwriting was becoming increasingly fierce, and his income was getting lower and lower.

With no other choice, Li Luo started sending out his resume everywhere, hoping to find another job with a stable salary.

Somehow, one of the resumes he submitted was for short video production, and as it happened, it was selected by Yan Zhusheng at the time.

The salary offered was very high, 8,000 a month, and Li Luo accepted the job without a second thought.

Only after meeting in person did he realize that Yan Zhusheng just played the piano and practiced singing in her spare time, casually recording some videos to upload. She didn't have any special requirements.

She just found the tedious tasks of video recording, shooting, and editing annoying and wanted to enjoy her music properly, so she simply found someone on a recruitment website.

The job was easy. Every day, he just helped Yan Zhusheng set up the camera, edit the videos, and then upload them.

There was plenty of free time, so Li Luo could also write short dramas to earn some extra cash on the side. His total monthly income could reach over 10,000, which was a relatively easy and comfortable period in his past life.

Later, Yan Zhusheng discovered that Li Luo could cook, and that his food was especially delicious, so she simply raised his salary to 15,000 and had him take care of daily meals as well.

Just like that, the two became more and more familiar. Li Luo even learned to play the guitar from Yan Zhusheng for free, and along the way, learned to play "Two Tigers" and "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" on the piano.

It was only later that Yan Zhusheng was diagnosed with a heart condition and needed to go abroad for treatment, which brought Li Luo's job to an unwilling end.

He originally thought it would be hard to meet her again after being reborn, but unexpectedly, right at the start of his first year of high school, Yan Zhusheng was sitting right beside him.

Li Luo glanced at Yan Zhusheng out of the corner of his eye, thinking that some fates were truly wonderful.

"You're looking at me." Yan Zhusheng turned her head and looked at Li Luo very seriously, as if she were simply solving a true-or-false question.

Li Luo was speechless.

This kind of straightforward innocence was truly the same as ever.

"You're good-looking. It's normal to look at you a bit more." Li Luo knew very well how to talk to Yan Zhusheng, so he admitted it directly, then gestured to their surroundings. "A lot of people are secretly looking at you."

"I know," Yan Zhusheng nodded.

It was unclear whether she knew she was good-looking, or knew that everyone else was looking at her...

Li Luo shook his head with a chuckle, retracted his gaze, and focused on the box his mom had stuffed into his hands earlier.

The small box was rectangular, the size of a palm, and wrapped in a layer of paper.

After Li Luo tore it open, the phone box inside was revealed, startling him so much that he shoved it into his desk drawer. He then looked up at the podium to confirm that Teacher Kong wasn't looking their way before lowering his head again.

An Android phone... a smartphone... It probably cost one or two thousand.

Li Luo recalled a joke he had made with his mom at the dinner table during the high school entrance exams.

He never expected that Lin Xiuhong would actually buy him a new phone.

He vaguely remembered that in his past life, his family didn't buy him a smartphone until after he finished the college entrance exams. Before that, they had always given him an old flip phone to use.

Thinking of this, Li Luo pursed his lips, a warm current flowing through his heart.

"Are we allowed to bring phones to school?" Yan Zhusheng asked, having glimpsed the phone box in his drawer.

"Shh, keep your voice down," Li Luo whispered. "In principle, we're definitely not allowed to bring them to school, but it's fine as long as the teachers don't find out."

"Oh." Yan Zhusheng nodded, indicating that she understood.

Li Luo took the phone box out of the drawer and stuffed it into his school bag, planning to fiddle with it when he got home that evening.

Just then, the last student in Class 8 finished registering.

Kong Junxiang organized the things on the podium, put all the tuition fees into a sealed bag, then stood up and looked at the whole class with a gentle smile. "Alright, now all forty students in our class are here."

"Welcome, everyone, to Fuyi High. My surname is Kong. You can call me Teacher Kong. From now on, I will be your head teacher."

Kong Junxiang gave a self-introduction and then explained the schedule for after registration. "We have three things to do this morning."

"Distributing student ID cards, self-introductions, and electing the class president, vice president, and the PE representatives for boys and girls."

"I, for one, don't like to waste time, so we'll combine these three things into one."

As he spoke, Kong Junxiang pulled a chair over to the doorway and sat down, holding a stack of student ID cards. He continued, "Now, when I call your name, come up here to get your student ID card, and then go to the stage for a self-introduction."

"After everyone has gotten their card and introduced themselves, those who want to run for class president, vice president, and PE representative can come up to campaign."

"If you have any questions, you can ask now."

After he finished speaking, the students looked at one another, and someone actually raised a hand.

"Go ahead," Kong Junxiang said, pointing at Xu Yinghuan who had her hand up.

"Teacher Kong, why are we only electing these few positions?" Xu Yinghuan asked sweetly. "Can I run for academic representative?"

"The other positions will be decided after the military training," Kong Junxiang explained with a smile. "Today, we're electing the four positions I mentioned first because during military training, we'll need them to serve the students. Any other questions?"

Apart from the naturally outgoing Xu Yinghuan, no one else in the class raised their hand.

So Kong Junxiang lowered his head, pulled out a student ID card, and then said, "Who is Hua Xiuxiu?"
